title: Tileset is corrupting resource paths when .godot directory is deleted
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD FirePro W2100 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.21026.2006) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600 CPU @ 3.50GHz (4 threads)

### Issue description

I'm unable to deliver a project I was working on to a client because every time I ship them the file, the texture path within the Tileset objects become corrupted.  This seems to be related to the .godot directory being either omitted or deleted.  

I had been omitting the .godot file from my deliverables since I was under the impression that this file just contained temporary files the Godot editor created during building and could be omitted.  

Anyhow, I describe the issue in detail in this thread:

https://forum.godotengine.org/t/godot-is-trashing-tileset-data-when-godot-directory-is-deleted/104264

Basically, when I started the project I created tilesets for a 32x16 iso tile set.  Then the client wanted to use 32x32 tileset instead so I created the new graphics and updated the tilesets.  However, deleting the .godot directory causes the Tilesets to revert to using the original tileset image resources.  I can't figure out why since I've searched  through all the files in the project and the original resources are not referenced anywhere.

Is there any way to fix this project so that I can delete/omit the .godot file and not have the Tilest resources corrupt?  Or am I misunderstanding how the .godot directory is meant to be used?

### Steps to reproduce

Open project.  Open tile_map_generator.tscn.  Make sure the tilesets are using textures from the /tilesets/iso_32x32 directory.  Close the project.  Delete the .godot file.  Reopen the project.  The Tilesets of some of the layers may have switched to using  the wrong texture resource.  (This is inconsistent; sometimes they corrupt, sometimes they don't).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I can't figure out how to come up with a minimal reproduction, so this is the whole thing.  I'm also including the .godot directory, since it's relevant to this issue.  

[dragonquest7worldbuilder.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19120354/dragonquest7worldbuilder.zip)
